articles.author: Sengi Runners
articles.description:
We build Sengi, a hosted runner service for GitHub Actions. Today we launched Sengi Basic, at $1 per 1,000 runner minutes. This post is about the idea behind it: pick the runner per job, not per company.
Look at a typical workflow run. Lint, unit tests, type checks, dependency audits, nightly jobs. Nobody is waiting on most of them. Then there are one or two jobs everyone is waiting on: the Docker image, the release build, the slow integration suite blocking a merge.
Paying the same per-minute rate for both makes no sense. So Sengi has two classes:



Size
Basic
Premium
GitHub-hosted Linux




2 vCPU
$0.001/min
$0.003/min
$0.006/min


4 vCPU
$0.002/min
$0.006/min
$0.012/min


8 vCPU
$0.004/min
$0.012/min
$0.022/min



Basic gives you six times the minutes per dollar of GitHub's own runners at 2 and 4 vCPU, and 5.5 times at 8 vCPU. 10,000 2-vCPU minutes cost $10 on Basic and $60 on GitHub at list price.
Premium is the fast class. On a PostHog Docker build at 4 vCPU it finished in 7m34s; GitHub's runner took 14m36s.
The class is just the label:
jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: sengi-basic-2-ubuntu-2404
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm ci && npm run lint

  test:
    runs-on: sengi-basic-4-ubuntu-2404
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm ci && npm test

  image:
    needs: test
    runs-on: sengi-premium-8-ubuntu-2404
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: docker build -t app .

Labels: sengi-basic-{2,4,8}-ubuntu-2404 and sengi-premium-{2,4,8}-ubuntu-2404. Workflows, secrets and logs stay in GitHub Actions.
Move every job to Basic.
Find the jobs where someone is waiting on the result.
Run those on Premium and compare time and cost against Basic.
Keep whichever wins for that job.
Every account gets 3,000 free Basic minutes a month. A 4-vCPU minute counts as two and an 8-vCPU minute as four.
More on Basic vs Premium: https://sengi.run/blog/sengi-basic-vs-premium
articles.title: Cheap runners for most CI jobs, fast runners for the few that matter

articles.author: Dzhem Hasan
articles.description:
A recurring question on Stack Overflow and
Manual Holiday Math: Distributed engineering teams have different national and regional public holidays. Manually subtracting days off per developer every sprint is error-prone.
Disconnected Time Logs & Capacity Bars: Capacity bars only work if Remaining Work and Completed Work stay synchronized as tasks move from Active to Resolved.
Cross-Project Blind Spots: Engineers shared across two repositories or project spaces appear at 100% capacity in both unless hours roll up centrally.
In VelocyTrack, we unified sprint capacity planning directly with the daily engineering backlog:
Automated Regional Holiday & Absence Deduction: Assign a country/state calendar per team member and record PTO once - available sprint hours recalculate automatically.
Real-Time Commitment vs. Capacity Gauge: See immediately whether a sprint is under-allocated, balanced, or over-committed across all 4 Azure DevOps process templates (Scrum, Agile, Basic, CMMI).
Zero Source Code Storage: Operates strictly on work item and Git metadata via AES-256 encrypted tokens.
You can explore a seeded sprint capacity & timelog workspace directly in your browser without signing up:
Explore the Live VelocyTrack Sandbox
articles.title: Sprint Capacity Planning in Azure DevOps: Handling Public Holidays, PTO, and Story-Level Rollups

這是 Claude Code 2.1.303 要求執行一個指令時，寫進終端機的內容。這些位元組來自一份真實的擷取，osFoundry 把它保留為測試 fixture（resources/agent-detection/fixtures/claude.blocked.raw）：
\r\x1b[1C\x1b[1B\x1b[39mDo\x1b[5Gyou\x1b[9Gwant\x1b[14Gto\x1b[17Gproceed?
\r\x1b[1C\x1b[1B\x1b[38;2;177;185;249m❯\x1b[4G\x1b[38;2;153;153;153m1. \x1b[38;2;177;185;249mYes
\r\x1b[3C\x1b[1B\x1b[38;2;153;153;153m2. \x1b[39mYes,\x1b[12Gand\x1b[16Galways\x1b[23Gallow ...

（為了方便閱讀加上了換行，原始擷取裡沒有換行。）
這段內容裡有兩件事，會讓最直覺的偵測方式失效。第一，「Do」和「you」之間沒有空白。\x1b[5G 把游標移到第 5 欄，那個「空白」只是一個沒被寫過的格子。第二，整段完全沒有 \n：每一列都是以 \r 加上游標下移的 \x1b[1B 開頭。fixture 資料夾裡全部 11 份 Claude Code 擷取（每份 2,099 到 7,672 位元組），沒有任何一個換行位元組。
osFoundry 的桌面應用程式會在 Sessions 看板上，替每一個終端機窗格回答「這個代理是不是在等我？」。以下說明它怎麼做、為什麼這樣做，再用一個小型 Python supervisor，在實際運作的 PTY 上比較三種常見做法（提示文字比對、輸出閒置計時、行程狀態）。這台 Mac 上沒有 claude 執行檔，所以即時測試的部分跑的是一個…

articles.description:
Live wallpaper apps like EWRE play a video behind your desktop icons, but in front of the static wallpaper. Windows has no public API for that. So how is it done?
This post explains the well-known technique that wallpaper engines use. It relies on undocumented shell behavior, so treat it as a field guide rather than a contract.
Your desktop is a stack of ordinary windows owned by Explorer:
Progman: the Program Manager window, the root of the desktop.
SHELLDLL_DefView: the window that draws your icons.
WorkerW: a helper window. The static wallpaper is painted into one of these.
The goal is to place your own window behind the icons (SHELLDLL_DefView) and in front of the static wallpaper.
Sending Progman an undocumented message, 0x052C, makes it spawn a WorkerW window sitting behind the icon …
articles.title: How Does a Live Wallpaper Draw Behind Your Desktop Icons on Windows?
